baseline.name: Minute-by-minute full grid rescans
baseline.approach: Scan every cell at each minute and stage newly rotten cells separately before the next minute.

archived.name: Multi-source BFS
archived.space: Fixed 100-entry queue under a 10x10 bound; generally O(m*n)

why: The queue visits only newly reachable cells and timestamps their propagation instead of rescanning the whole grid per minute.
quantitative_comparison: Each grid cell enters the archived queue at most once. The baseline can inspect m*n cells during each of d minutes; this avoids a factor of repeated full scans in the work model, not a measured d-times speedup.
tradeoffs: The archive mutates the input and has a fixed queue capacity. d=0 or tiny grids may show little elapsed benefit; the zero-latency source comment is not a measurement.
evidence_basis: Static BFS enqueue invariant versus the defined synchronous-rescan baseline; no timing benchmark.
